replies.body: Same thing confused me for a whole evening Check `main.jsx` — you'll see `<StrictMode>` wrapping your app. Run `npm run build && npm run preview` and it fires once.
Pro tip from my last internship: interviewers *love* asking this. Remember the phrase "StrictMode double-invokes effects in dev to surface missing cleanups".
I charged ₹1,500 for my first one and regretted it, took 3 weeks of revisions. Quote higher than you think!

Congratulations on your first client! Here's how I'd think about it:

**1. Price the package, not the hours.** For a local café: logo + 2 colour variants + social avatar is a *starter brand kit*.

**2. Ballpark for a beginner in a tier-2 city:** ₹3,000–₹6,000. Quote **₹4,500** and leave room to give a "student discount" to ₹4,000 if he pushes.

**3. Put limits in writing:**
- 3 initial concepts
- 2 rounds of revisions
- Final files: PNG, SVG, PDF
- 50% advance on UPI before you start

**4. Show, don't tell.** Send a one-page PDF with your process (moodboard → sketches → final). Owners pay more when they see a process.

You've got this. Post the final logo in the portfolio once it's done!
Saving this. The 50% advance part is gold — learnt it the hard way
Also add a line that he can't ask for a whole new concept after round 2 — otherwise it never ends. Worked for me on my first web client.

Very common, and very fixable. Founders say "unlimited" because they're scared of getting bad work — not because they want 15 drafts. Address the fear, then set the limit.

Try something like:

> "Totally get it — you want posts that sound like you. Here's how I'll make sure of that: before writing, I'll send a 5-line outline for your approval. After that, each post includes **2 revision rounds** within 7 days. If we need a full rewrite because the direction changed, that's billed as a new post. This keeps both of us fast."

The outline step is the magic. 90% of revisions happen because the brief was fuzzy.
Bhai, mention it in the invoice too. "Includes 2 revisions" — once it's on paper nobody argues.
+1 to Debjani. Also send a quick Loom/voice note explaining your first draft. Clients revise less when they understand your reasoning.
JOIN is always faster, subqueries are slow. Use JOIN.

"Always" is not quite right Your correlated subquery runs `AVG` once **per student row** (unless the optimizer rewrites it). The cleaner pattern is to compute each department's average **once** and join to it:

```sql
WITH dept_avg AS (
  SELECT dept_id, AVG(marks) AS avg_marks
  FROM students
  GROUP BY dept_id
)
SELECT s.name, s.marks
FROM students s
JOIN dept_avg d ON d.dept_id = s.dept_id
WHERE s.marks > d.avg_marks;
```

For a college dataset of 500 rows you'll see no difference. On 5 lakh rows, the CTE + JOIN wins. Write the CTE version and add one line in your answer explaining *why* — that's what gets you full marks.
Ohh the CTE version is so much more readable too. Thank you sir!

Honest answer: **Canva is enough to start earning, not enough to grow.**

- Social posts, fest posters, simple reels covers → Canva is perfect, and clients care about results.
- Logos, brand identities, packaging, anything that gets printed big → you need vector tools.

You don't need Adobe right now. Learn **Figma** (free) or **Inkscape** (free) for vector work. The skills (pen tool, boolean shapes, grids) transfer 1:1 to Illustrator later.

Plan: keep earning with Canva, spend 30 min a day on vector basics. In 6 weeks you'll be quoting for logos.
I do ₹600–₹1,200 Canva gigs for local coaching centres every month. Canva is totally fine for that market
Figma for vectors is underrated. The Campus UI/UX track has a pen tool lesson, check it out.

Love this brief! Premium Hinglish = **fewer words, one Hindi hook, no exclamation spam.**

Rewrites:
- *"Haath se chhapa, dil se pehna. Block-printed in Jaipur, made for your Sunday plans."*
- *"Dadi ki almirah wali feeling, but make it 2026."*
- *"Indigo, sanganeri, aur thoda sa sukoon."*

Rules I follow:
1. One Hindi phrase that carries emotion, rest in clean English
2. Max one emoji, and only if it adds meaning
3. Use sensory words: *haath se, mitti, dhoop, sukoon*
4. Read it out loud — if your mom would roll her eyes, cut it
"Dadi ki almirah wali feeling" this is so good. Stealing the read-aloud rule.
From the ads side: test 2–3 caption styles as Reels captions for a week and see which one gets more saves. Saves = premium audience signal.
It was a decorative blur circle for me `-right-20` on an absolute div. `overflow-x-hidden` on the section fixed it.

Nice first campaign! For ₹5,000 over ~10 days:

- **Days 1–3 · ₹1,500** → test 3 creatives (Reel, carousel, static)
- **Days 4–10 · ₹3,500** → put everything on the winner

**Targeting:** Lucknow + 8 km radius, 24–45, interests: gifting, Diwali, home bakers. Keep it broad — Meta's algorithm is smarter than manual interests now.

**Objective:** Messages (WhatsApp click-to-chat). Home bakeries close sales in DMs, not on websites.

Track one number: **cost per WhatsApp conversation**. Under ₹40 is good for hampers.
Use real photos of the hampers, not Canva mockups. Real kitchen photos convert way better for home bakers.

Been there — I edited my first 50 videos on a ₹35k laptop. Do these in order:

1. **Proxies.** Right-click clips → Proxy → Create Proxies (ProRes 422 Proxy or H.264 720p). Toggle the proxy button in the monitor. This alone fixes 80%.
2. Playback resolution → **1/4**.
3. Close Chrome. Seriously. 30 tabs = 3GB RAM.
4. Media cache on your fastest drive, clean it monthly.
5. Phone footage is often *variable frame rate* — convert with HandBrake to constant 30fps first.

Your export will still be full 4K quality. Proxies only affect editing.
Proxies changed my life. Also try CapCut desktop for short reels, it's very light.

Simple version:

- **Hug contents** → "be as big as what's inside me" (like a button around its label)
- **Fill container** → "stretch to take all the space my parent gives me"
- **Fixed** → "I don't care, I'm exactly 240px"

For a card: the **card** is Fixed width (say 320), Hug height. The **image** is Fill width, Fixed height (180). The **text** is Fill width, Hug height. The **button** is Hug both.

Your image stretches because it's probably on Fill height. Set it to Fixed and it'll stop. Want me to look at your file? Book a free slot with me

Classic one. Check these:

1. Add **both SHA-1 and SHA-256** — debug *and* release keys. Get them with `./gradlew signingReport`.
2. Download the **new** `google-services.json` after adding the keys and replace the old file.
3. Enable **Play Integrity API** in Google Cloud console for the same project.
4. Redmi/MIUI: make sure Chrome is updated — the reCAPTCHA fallback opens in Chrome.

Then `flutter clean && flutter run`. 9 out of 10 times it's step 2.
It was step 2!! I had the old json Thank you so much Kiran sir.
Content writing! Got my first ₹800 gig in 3 weeks. If you can write decent English (or Hindi), start there.

Coming from commerce is actually an advantage — you understand margins, customers and selling. Fastest routes I've seen for B.Com students:

1. **Digital marketing** — local businesses (coaching centres, clinics, cafés) need someone to run Instagram and Google Business. First gig in 3–5 weeks is common.
2. **Content writing** — product descriptions, blogs. Low barrier, steady.
3. **Data analytics (Excel + Power BI)** — slower start, but your accounting knowledge makes you stand out.

Start with 1 or 2, aim for Stage 3 (micro-gigs) on the Earn Ladder in a month. And don't compare with the coding crowd — clients pay for outcomes, not for languages.
B.Com here too, doing Instagram for 2 clinics now at ₹4k each/month. Digital marketing 100%.
Yes! Shopify/Meesho sellers with 200+ products would love this. Try charging per 100 descriptions instead of a flat fee.

Don't panic, do this in order:

1. **Revoke the key right now** in the OpenAI dashboard. Assume it's already leaked — bots scan GitHub in minutes.
2. Create a new key, put it in `.env`, and add `.env` to `.gitignore`.
3. Optionally clean history with `git filter-repo --path .env --invert-paths` and force push.

Step 1 is the only one that really matters. History cleaning is nice-to-have; a revoked key is useless to anyone.
Happened to me with a Firebase key. Also add a `.env.example` with empty values so teammates know what's needed.

Write **spec pieces for real brands** you like — clearly labelled "spec work":

- Rewrite the About page of a local brand you love
- Write 3 product descriptions for a D2C brand on Instagram
- A blog post for a SaaS tool you actually use

Then submit them as Campus assignments — once a mentor reviews them, they show up as **verified** in your Proof Portfolio. That carries more weight than "samples" in a Google Doc.
Did exactly this — the verified tag on my portfolio got me 2 interviews. Works.

Recruiters skim, so structure for skimming:

1. **Hero**: final screens + one-line outcome ("cut order time from 4 min to 90 sec")
2. **Problem** (3 lines + one real quote from a classmate)
3. **Process** — 3–4 images max: research → wireframes → iterations
4. **Final UI** + one thing you'd improve

~800 words, lots of visuals. If they're interested in minute one, they'll read the rest.
The canteen idea is so relatable. Post the link when it's done!

Great real-world project! For a shop owner, keep it to **5 cards**:

1. **Today vs same day last week** sales
2. **Top 10 items by profit** (not revenue!)
3. **Slow movers** — stock that hasn't sold in 30 days (cash stuck on shelves)
4. **Peak hours heatmap** — when to have extra help
5. **Udhaar (credit) outstanding** by customer

Make it work on his phone (Power BI mobile layout). If he opens it every morning, that's your case study headline.
Udhaar tracking he will LOVE that. Thanks Arvind sir!
The chai analogy made it click. Thanks Aarav!
Great explanation One more: for 1,000 requests, don't fire them all at once — batch them (e.g. 10 at a time) or you'll hit rate limits.

2 seconds means the **first frame** isn't doing its job. Editing checklist for hooks:

- **Start mid-action.** Cut the "Hey guys". First frame = the most interesting moment.
- **Text hook in frame 1**, big, max 6 words: *"You're doing squats wrong"*.
- **Pattern interrupt every 2–3 sec**: zoom punch-in, angle change, B-roll.
- **Captions** always — 80% watch on mute.
- **Loop the ending** into the start so replays count.

Then A/B test hooks: same reel, 2 different first 2 seconds. Data > opinions.
Zoom punch-ins on beats are so effective. I use 110% scale keyframes on every cut.

Congrats! Polite negotiation almost never gets an offer withdrawn. Try:

> "I'm really excited about this role. Given my portfolio work on [X] and that I can work 5 days a week, would ₹12k be possible?"

If they can't move on money, ask for: a PPO conversation at month 4, a learning budget, or remote Fridays. Worst case they say no and you still have ₹8k.
Did the same last year, asked for 12, got 10. Always ask

Add a queue (even a simple in-memory one) and retry with exponential backoff on 429s. Also cache reviews — many students upload the same template resume! A smaller, cheaper model for a first pass helps too.
We used `p-limit` in Node to cap concurrency at 3. Solved it for our hackathon.
Ugh, sorry. Happened to me too. Send a polite reminder with the UPI QR every 3 days.

Sorry this happened — it's a rite of passage, unfortunately. Now:

1. One clear, friendly message: *"Hi! Sharing the invoice again for the logo project. Could you clear ₹2,500 by Friday? Happy to help with anything else you need."*
2. If no reply in a week, a firmer one mentioning that usage rights transfer after payment.

**Next time:**
- 50% advance, always
- Send **watermarked previews**; final source files only after full payment
- Work through Campus gigs where payment is held safely

You did the work. Don't let this one stop you.
He paid after the second message Thank you Meghna ma'am. Watermarks from now on.

Use **content pillars** + a batching day:

- Pillar 1: Education (myth vs fact, tips)
- Pillar 2: Trust (doctor intro, patient stories, clinic tour)
- Pillar 3: Offers (check-up camps, festive offers)
- Pillar 4: Community (health days, local events)

12 posts/month = 3 per pillar. One Sunday: write all captions in a sheet, design in Canva with a template, schedule in Meta Business Suite. 4 hours total, done for the month.

Both are fine; pick based on what you already know and the clients you want:

- **Flutter**: very popular with Indian agencies and startups building MVPs; one codebase looks identical everywhere.
- **React Native**: great if you already do React web — clients love one person who can do web + app.

You know JS → React Native gets you earning faster. But honestly, the freelancer who **ships and communicates well** wins, not the framework.
Flutter gigs on Campus gigs board are more frequent this month fwiw.
Message the clients today — not on Tuesday night. Most will give 3–4 extra days if you tell them early. Exams are a valid reason.
Rule I give all my mentees: never hide a delay. Communicate early, offer a partial delivery, and protect your sleep. You'll do better in both.

Honest answer: **haan, milegi — agar aap prep years ko explain karna aur ek skill ka proof dikhana seekh lo.**

Companies "gap" se nahi darti, unhe darr hota hai ki candidate kaam nahi kar paayega. Aapke paas already hai:
- **Discipline** — 3 saal roz ka schedule
- **Hindi + English** — bilingual log kam milte hain, translation aur content mein demand hai
- **Research skill** — current affairs ke notes banana = research

Mera suggestion: roz 45 minute translation track, aur 2 mahine mein 3 samples (ek press release, ek brochure, ek subtitle file). Phir pehle micro-gigs. Taiyari chhodne ki zaroorat nahi — yeh backup hai.

IBPS PO ki 2 saal taiyari ki thi. Tally + GST seekha, abhi ek CA firm mein accounts executive hoon, ₹22k/month se start. Interview mein kisi ne gap pe taunt nahi kiya, bas poocha 'kya seekha'. Aap kar logi
UPSC ke 4 saal ke baad main bhi yahi soch raha tha. Campus pe content writing aur translation dono chal rahe hain. Sabse badi baat: akela nahi lagta ab.
Same problem bro. I just say 'preparing for govt exams' and move on quickly

Don't apologise — **explain, then bridge**. Use a 3-part answer, about 40 seconds:

1. **The fact, said with confidence:** "I prepared for SSC CGL for three years and cleared Tier 1 twice."
2. **What it built:** "It taught me to study 6–8 hours a day on a fixed schedule, analyse 200+ mock tests and fix my weak areas — that's exactly what MIS work is: data, deadlines and accuracy."
3. **The bridge to this job:** "Alongside, I learned Excel — lookups, pivots, MIS reports — and here's a report I built on a DI dataset."

Then **show the proof**: your Skill Passport link with the reviewed assignment. An interviewer remembers the workbook, not the gap.

Practise it aloud 10 times. It should sound like a story, not a defence.
Sir ka 3-part answer maine apni diary mein likh liya. Ek cheez add karungi: 'Preparation record' Skill Passport pe dikhta hai, toh HR ko pehle se pata hota hai. Thank you!

Good question, Pooja — and the Excel 2016 detail is the key.

- **XLOOKUP** is better: it looks left or right, defaults to exact match and has a built-in "not found" value. But it exists only in **Excel 2021 / 365** (and Google Sheets).
- **VLOOKUP** works everywhere, including Excel 2016. Always use `FALSE` (exact match) and wrap it: `=IFERROR(VLOOKUP(A2, Retailers!A:C, 2, FALSE), "Not found")`.

For the assignment: use XLOOKUP and add one note in your Summary sheet saying the VLOOKUP version for older Excel. Clients love that you thought about their computer. In interviews, say you know both.
INDEX + MATCH bhi seekh lo, purane office files mein bahut milta hai. Excel 2016 pe bhi left lookup ho jaata hai.
Tally first. CA firms mein 90% Tally hi chalta hai, job ke liye bhi wahi poochte hain.

Both are good; here's how I'd decide:

- **Tally Prime** — the default in CA firms and most job descriptions ("Tally operator", "accounts executive"). Learn this first for employability.
- **Busy** — popular with traders and distributors in North India for inventory and billing. Once you know accounting, switching takes a week; the vouchers and ledgers are the same idea.

**Pricing for a small shop (monthly bookkeeping):** ₹1,500–₹3,000 for up to ~150 vouchers a month, more if you also prepare GST return data for their CA. Fix the scope in writing: number of bills, a weekly visit or WhatsApp photos, and a monthly deadline.

Start with one shop, do it perfectly for 2 months, and ask for a referral.

For a beginner with your writing background:

- **General content (NGO reports, blogs):** ₹0.80–₹1.20 per word → ₹1,600–₹2,400 for 2,000 words.
- **Legal / technical:** ₹1.50–₹2.50 per word, because accuracy risk is higher.
- **Minimum charge:** ₹500 per job, even for 100 words.

Ask for the reference material and any glossary they already use, agree on one revision round, and send a 150-word sample first. NGOs often have recurring work, so a good first job leads to monthly orders.
Main ₹1/word se start kiya tha, 3rd client se ₹1.20. Glossary banao, consistency se client khush rehta hai.

criteria.label: Meets the brief

criteria.label: Usability

criteria.guide: Spacing, type, colour and hierarchy are consistent and intentional.

criteria.label: Usability and accessibility
criteria.guide: Flows are clear; labels, empty/error states and contrast (WCAG AA) work for real users.

criteria.label: Design rationale
criteria.guide: A short case-study note explains the problem, the choices and what you would test next.

criteria.label: Handover
criteria.guide: Files are organised, named and shareable. A developer or client can use them as they are.

criteria.label: Requirements met
criteria.guide: Every feature in the brief works. Nothing core is missing or broken.

criteria.label: Code quality
criteria.guide: Readable structure, sensible names, no copy-paste blocks, no secrets in the repo.

criteria.label: Responsive and tested
criteria.guide: Works on a 375px phone and desktop. Forms validate. No console errors.

criteria.label: README and decisions
criteria.guide: A README says how to run it and why key choices were made.

criteria.label: Live and handed over
criteria.guide: A live link opens and the repo can be handed to a client.

criteria.label: Fits the brief and audience
criteria.guide: The plan or copy speaks to the stated audience and goal.

criteria.label: Copy and creative quality
criteria.guide: Clear, specific, on-brand. Hooks and calls to action are strong.

criteria.label: Measurement plan
criteria.guide: Says what will be tracked, the target and how success is judged.

criteria.label: Honest claims
criteria.guide: No false or unprovable claims; ad and platform policies are respected.

criteria.label: Meets the brief
criteria.guide: Length, format and message match the brief.

criteria.label: Hook and pacing
criteria.guide: Holds attention in the first two seconds; cuts are deliberate.

criteria.label: Technical quality
criteria.guide: Clean audio, readable captions, correct export settings, no glitches.

criteria.label: Delivery
criteria.guide: Files are named, exported for each platform and shared with working links.

criteria.label: Accuracy
criteria.guide: Figures, entries or translations are correct. Errors would cost a client money or trust.

criteria.label: Method
criteria.guide: Uses the right tool features (formulas, vouchers, glossary) rather than manual work.

criteria.label: Presentation
criteria.guide: Clean layout, clear labels; a client can read it without help.

criteria.label: Delivery and notes
criteria.guide: Delivered in the requested format with a short note on assumptions.
